content:
The Guardian reports that Apple is in talks with several companies to acquire the US broadcasting rights for The Open Championship. Sources indicate that Netflix and Amazon are also expected to express interest in these broadcasting rights.

The Open Championship, which began in Scotland in 1860, is the oldest of the four men's major golf tournaments and is organised by the R&A. Americans generally refer to it as the "British Open" to distinguish it from the other major, the US Open.

NBC secured the broadcasting rights for The Open Championship in 2017 with a 12-year deal, having beaten ESPN in the process. The broadcasting rights are jointly held by NBC and Versant, with the latter operating the Golf Channel. The R&A said it expects to hold discussions with NBC, Versant, and other parties interested in the broadcasting rights.

The latest report states that Apple has initiated "preliminary discussions" with the R&A regarding a bid for The Open Championship. The report cited an "informed source" and noted that Apple "remains committed to investing in sports broadcasting rights and will continue to seek out suitable sports assets".

An R&A spokesperson responded to The Guardian's inquiry, stating:

"Our partnerships with NBC and Versant have been outstanding, delivering exceptional results for The Open, the AIG Women's Open, as well as our other championships and international events. Looking ahead to the next R&A media rights cycle in the United States, we anticipate engaging with our existing partners NBC and Versant in due course, while continuing to monitor developments in the broadcasting industry and the level of interest from various parties in our rights."

Apple announced last year that it had become the exclusive US broadcasting partner for Formula 1 (F1). The company also broadcasts Friday Night Baseball and Major League Soccer (MLS) matches.
